subject: Prospective PhD applicant (Fall 2027): understanding and control in AI that acts on personal data
body:
Dear Prof. Li,

I'm a product data analyst at a consumer fitness app, and I'm applying to the Khoury HCI PhD program for Fall 2027. I'm writing because your lab's work is closer than anything else I've found to the question I want to study.

Our app recently launched an AI feature that rewrites people's workout plans using their sleep, activity, and heart-rate data. By our metrics it was a success. But when I coded the open-ended survey responses after launch, I kept finding people who said it had changed their plan and they had no idea why. Some asked how it knew they had slept badly, and a few turned off health-data sharing. None of that showed up in the headline numbers. I want to understand what people think is happening when an app uses their own data to decide things for them, and what would make them feel they still have a say.

I'm still new to the research literature. When I found the PEACH Lab site, its focus on human-centered approaches to privacy in AI, ones that empower people rather than only improving models, matched what I'd been trying to put into words. I'm especially curious how questions of control and oversight play out for AI that acts quietly in the background, outside a chat interface.

My background is mostly quantitative: four years of experiment analysis, plus undergraduate HCI research projects. I don't have publications yet, and qualitative methods are what I most want to train in.

Are you planning to take new PhD students this cycle? I'm happy to send my CV if you'd like it, and I'd be grateful for any chance to talk.

Best regards,
Riley Nakamura
